newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico gov't says sees '96 CPI at half '95 level.
newsitem.headline: Mexico gov't says sees '96 CPI at half '95 level.

text.p: Mexico's rate of inflation during 1996 should be less than half the rate of inflation during the previous year, a government spokesman said on Wednesday.

Alejandro Valenzuela, spokesman for the government's economic recovery program, told a news conference that despite a slight rise in inflation during September, inflation should resume its downward trend during the year's final months.

"Because of seasonal factors, inflation during September should be slightly higher than inflation during August. But it is undeniable that during October and November we should see inflation begin to fall again, which will allow us to have inflation (during 1996) of less than half what we had last year," Valenzuela said.
Valenzuela said higher education prices from the start of the school year should push up inflation during September versus the 1.33 percent recorded in August.
"No one should be surprised that September's inflation rate is slightly higher than August," he said.
